Done. I've created a complete Go todo list CLI in `/home/hebin/todoapp-demo`.

## What I built

**Files:**
- `go.mod` — module `github.com/example/todoapp`, `go 1.21`
- `main.go` — single `main` package with subcommands `add`, `list`, `done`, `rm`

**Task model** (JSON in `./todos.json` next to the binary):
- `id` (int)
- `title` (string)
- `done` (bool)
- `created_at` (timestamp, RFC3339 via `time.Now()`)

**Behavior:**
- `add <title>` — appends a task with auto-incrementing ID
- `list` — sorts by ID ascending, shows `[ ]` / `[x]` status
- `done <id>` — marks a task done
- `rm <id>` — removes a task
- Tasks are read/written as indented JSON; a missing/empty file is treated as an empty list; unknown commands and missing/invalid args get clear errors.

**Verification:** Both `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` succeed (confirmed on the final run), and I exercised every subcommand end-to-end — add, list, done, rm, and verified the persisted JSON structure with a real timestamp. I cleaned up the test `todos.json` afterwards, so fresh `todoapp add` calls will start from scratch.
